QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.474 on Nov 18, slightly below 0.5, the independent, finite-variance reference. R²=0.933 measures fit only at tested scales. Short/long slopes (0.471/0.599) differ: one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, suggesting possible crossover or temporary volatility change. Magnitude H=0.770 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell from 0.520 on Nov 6. Its 1/5-observation changes were +0.009/−0.004. The prior-30 standardized deviation was −0.24, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha rose from 3.198 on Nov 5 to 3.490 on Nov 16–18. Plateaus are normal without new top-k extremes. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner absolute-return tails if the model fits. The 1,000-return window uses k=100 and x_min=0.02043 absolute log-return units. The idealized independent-return SE (alpha/√k) is 0.349 and understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.583/3.019, not a confidence interval. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
